verified_claims: Substituting x=f(y) is legitimate because f(y)>0; both outer terms collapse to f(y), forcing equality in the middle and hence f(f(y))=2f(y)-y for all y>0.
With g(x)=f(x)-x, the relation f(f(y))=2f(y)-y is equivalently g(y+g(y))=g(y); induction then gives g(x+n g(x))=g(x) and f^n(x)=x+n g(x) for all nonnegative integers n.
Since every iterate f^n(x) is positive, x+n g(x)>0 for all n; this rules out g(x)<0, so g(x)>=0 everywhere.
The two squared-defect computations are correct and combine to the two-sided bound |g(x)-g(y)|(2x+2y+g(x)+g(y)) <= (x-y-g(y))^2 for all x,y>0.

If g attained two distinct positive values A and B at x and y, then for n large one can choose m>=0 with x+nA-y-mB-B bounded; the defect bound then has left side growing linearly in n while the right side stays bounded, a contradiction. Thus g has at most one positive value.

If the range of g were {0,c} with c>0, the cross-level inequality c(2x+2y+c)<=(x-y)^2 gives uniform positive separation of each c-level point from the zero level and of each zero-level point from the c-level; hence both level sets would be open in (0,infty), contradicting connectedness.
Therefore g is constant c>=0 and f(x)=x+c. These functions indeed map positive reals to positive reals and satisfy the chain by QM-AM-GM applied to the positive numbers x and y+c.
summary: The proof is sound and complete. The key collapse at x=f(y), the linearization g=f-id, positivity of iterates, and the exact squared-defect identity all check out. The orbit approximation excludes two distinct positive values of g, and the separation estimate makes a two-value range {0,c} impossible by connectedness. The claimed family f(x)=x+c, c>=0, verifies exactly by QM-AM-GM.
